explanation: Each response fits its hunter. Climbing a tree escapes a leopard but exposes a monkey to an eagle, while snake calls make vervets stand tall and search the grass.

claims.text: On hearing an eagle alarm call, vervet monkeys look up and run into dense bushes.
Vervets respond to eagle alarm calls by taking cover in bushes, not by climbing trees, searching the grass or freezing.
Vervet monkeys give different alarm calls for leopards, eagles and snakes.
Vervets climb trees on hearing a leopard alarm call, which protects them from leopards but not from eagles.
On hearing a snake alarm call, vervets stand up on their hind legs and scan the ground.

evidence.restatement: When vervets hear the eagle alarm they look up and run into dense bushes.
Climbing trees is the leopard response, scanning the ground is the snake response, and freezing is not the eagle response.
Vervet monkeys use distinct alarm calls for leopards, eagles and snakes.
On a leopard alarm vervets climb into trees, out of a leopard's reach but exposed to an eagle.
On a snake alarm vervets stand up on their hind legs and scan the ground around them.
Vervet monkeys answer an eagle alarm by looking up and running into dense bushes.

claimResults.note: Classic field-playback result: leopard call, climb into trees; eagle call, look up and take cover in bushes; snake call, stand and scan the ground.

evidence.restatement: The eagle response is cover in bushes; trees are the leopard response and scanning the ground the snake response.
Vervets give distinct alarm calls for leopards, eagles and snakes.
A leopard alarm sends vervets up into trees, which would be a poor refuge from an eagle.
A snake alarm makes vervets stand on their hind legs and look at the ground.
